3
Calipers are used to determine the thickness of the wall of a glass tube.
wall
glass tube
The following measurements are made.
internal diameter of the tube = (10.0 ± 0.1) mm
external diameter of the tube = (12.0 ± 0.1) mm
What is the thickness of the wall of the tube?
A
(1.0 ± 0.1) mm
B
(1.0 ± 0.2) mm
C
(2.0 ± 0.1) mm
D
(2.0 ± 0.2) mm

hints: Notice the diagram shows the wall on both sides of the hollow tube, so external diameter minus internal diameter equals two wall thicknesses.
Recall that for addition or subtraction the absolute uncertainties in $(10.0 \pm 0.1)\text{ mm}$ and $(12.0 \pm 0.1)\text{ mm}$ must be added.
Check what happens to both the value and its absolute uncertainty when you divide that diameter difference by the exact number 2.
walkthrough: Identify the geometry from the diagram: external diameter = internal diameter + 2 x wall thickness, so $t = (D - d)/2$.
Substitute the values with units: $D - d = 12.0\text{ mm} - 10.0\text{ mm} = 2.0\text{ mm}$.
Combine absolute uncertainties for subtraction by addition: $\Delta(D-d) = 0.1\text{ mm} + 0.1\text{ mm} = 0.2\text{ mm}$, so difference $= (2.0 \pm 0.2)\text{ mm}$.
Divide by the exact number 2: $t = 2.0/2 = 1.0\text{ mm}$ and $\Delta t = 0.2/2 = 0.1\text{ mm}$.
Unit check gives $\text{mm}$ throughout, so thickness $= (1.0 \pm 0.1)\text{ mm}$. This is option A.

A.explanation: Wall thickness is half the diameter difference, $(12.0-10.0)/2 = 1.0\text{ mm}$, with halved combined uncertainty $0.2/2 = 0.1\text{ mm}$.

B.explanation: Value $1.0\text{ mm}$ is correct but $0.2\text{ mm}$ forgets that dividing the $2.0\text{ mm}$ difference by 2 also halves its absolute uncertainty.

C.explanation: It uses the full diameter difference $12.0-10.0 = 2.0\text{ mm}$ and misses that the wall appears on both sides so must be halved.

D.explanation: It gives only the diameter difference $2.0\text{ mm}$ with added uncertainty $0.2\text{ mm}$, without dividing by 2 for the single wall thickness.
